title: State Corporation Commission approves new Dominion rate changes for big electricity users
description: The State Corporation Commission (SCC) has approved the creation of a new rate class for the biggest users of electricity for Dominion Energy, including data centers. The new GS-5 rate class, comprising customers demanding 25 megawatts or more, will go in to effect January 1, 2027. Certain large-scale customers will be required to pay a minimum of 85% of contracted distribution and transmission demand, and 60% of generation demand, says the SCC. The SCC says Dominion Energy wanted base-rate increases of $822 million in 2026 and $345 million for 2027, but evidence only supported an increase of $565.7 million in 2026 and $209.9 million in 2027. The Commission also approved an increase in Dominion’s authorized return on equity from 9.7% to 9.8%, less than the company’s requested return of 10.4%. These new rate changes will result in monthly increases of $11.24 in 2026 and $2.36 in 2027. title: Granbury City Council, March 3, 2026: City Manager Recognizes City Staff
description: Granbury City Manager Chris Coffman recognized two new City employees: John Copeland, the new Assistant City Manager. and Chris Sharp, the new Director of City Projects. He will also hold the title of Interim Public Works Director.   Coffman recognized the following promotions: Ty Gregg, from Granbury PD officer to Corporal; Robert Bright, promoted to full-time patrol officer; and, Aubrey Edwards, who qualified to become a Code Enforcement Officer.  Coffman then recognized Electric Utility Director Kenneth Causey and Purchasing Director Christy Russell for working together on many projects along Hwy. 377 section from Pirate Drive to Overstreet Way. One in particular was the purchase of two metal poles to be in Granbury in time for the October 1 deadline for moving all utilities.   Chris Sharpe gathered all information, letters and forms necessary to meet a tight deadline and submit an application for funding from the federal government.  Mayor Jim Jarratt, Finance Director Eva Gregory and other directors help with input and gathering of information.  Coffman recognized Economic Development Director Shea Hopkins in her work with citizens who are asking questions about the recent news surrounding data centers coming to Granbury and Hood County. Coffman also recognized Hopkins and her staff for their work putting together a list of compliances and enforcements for companies that want to come to Granbury.
